Treat premises as assumptions, cite exact supplied-source locations for the control and effect, preserve decisive unknowns, and do not execute the target or infer deployment facts.

publicBrief.acceptedPolicy: Creating a note requires the POST global note/document permissions and an owner-aware change_document check on the target document; viewing the document alone is insufficient.
publicBrief.currentQuestion: At DocumentViewSet.notes POST handler entry, can an authenticated user who has all listed global POST permissions and an object view grant on a document create a note when a different user owns the document and the caller has no object change_document grant?
premises: At notes POST entry, the authenticated caller has the global POST permissions and an object view grant, but is not the document owner and lacks its object change_document grant.
requiredResponseDetails: Separate the global PaperlessNotePermissions check, the object view check, the object change check, and Note.objects.create effect.

results.explanation: At the declared notes POST entry, the source exposes PaperlessNotePermissions as the action-level permission class, but the supplied crop does not include that class's implementation; the task premise supplies that the global POST permissions are satisfied. The handler binds the authenticated caller as request.user and binds the target document by pk, including its owner, then performs an owner-aware view check. Under the stated premise that the caller has object view access, that check does not deny. In the POST path, however, the handler performs a separate owner-aware change_document check on the same document. The premise says the caller lacks that object change grant and is not the owner, so this check returns HttpResponseForbidden before Note.objects.create is reached. Therefore the source-visible behavior at the declared boundary is deny. The protected effect is note creation, and it is not reached. No decisive runtime fact is missing for this source-path assessment because the entry assumptions provide the global, view, ownership, and missing-change facts; deployment behavior and the unshown PaperlessNotePermissions implementation are outside the supplied boundary and are not needed to establish the visible object-change denial path.

entry.statement: The notes action is declared for POST and uses PaperlessNotePermissions.

binding.statement: The handler binds the caller from request.user.
The handler resolves the target document from pk and loads its owner identity.

control.statement: The POST path separately requires an owner-aware change_document check on the target document and returns HTTP 403 when that check fails.

The action-level global permission gate is declared through PaperlessNotePermissions; its implementation is not present in the supplied crop, while satisfaction of the listed global permissions is an accepted task premise.
Before method dispatch, the handler performs an owner-aware view_document check and forbids access if it fails; the stated object-view premise makes this check non-blocking for the scenario.

effect.statement: Note.objects.create would create the note only after the change_document check; it is therefore unreachable under the stated missing object-change grant.
